# kafka_quota (Resource)

Kafka client quota: the rate limits that apply to one entity (a user, a client id, a combination of the two, or an IP address). Requires Kafka 2.6 or later.

The entity is fixed: changing it replaces the quota. The limits are updated in place. Only the limits set in the configuration are managed; a limit that is set on the broker but not in the configuration is left alone.

Use `user` and `client_id` together or alone, or `ip` alone. At least one limit is required. Kafka only accepts `connection_creation_rate` for an `ip` entity and the other limits for `user` and `client_id` entities.

The id has the form `user=alice,client-id=billing` (types in the order `user`, `client-id`, `ip`, names URL-escaped, the default entity written as `<default>`), and is what `terraform import` takes.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Limit one user's traffic through one client application.
resource "kafka_quota" "billing" {
  user      = { name = "alice" }
  client_id = { name = "billing" }

  producer_byte_rate = 1048576
  consumer_byte_rate = 2097152
  request_percentage = 25
}

# Apply a default to every client id that has no quota of its own.
resource "kafka_quota" "default_client" {
  client_id = { default = true }

  producer_byte_rate = 524288
}

# Limit new connections from one IP address.
resource "kafka_quota" "office" {
  ip = { name = "203.0.113.7" }

  connection_creation_rate = 10
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `client_id` (Attributes) The client id the quota applies to. Can be combined with `user`, not with `ip`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--client_id))
- `connection_creation_rate` (Number) Maximum number of connections per second the entity may create, per broker. Only supported with `ip`. Must not be negative. Remove the attribute to remove the limit.
- `consumer_byte_rate` (Number) Maximum bytes per second the entity may fetch, per broker. Must not be negative. Remove the attribute to remove the limit.
- `controller_mutation_rate` (Number) Maximum rate of partition creations and deletions the entity may cause, in partitions per second. Must not be negative. Remove the attribute to remove the limit.
- `ip` (Attributes) The IP address the quota applies to. Cannot be combined with `user` or `client_id`, and only supports `connection_creation_rate`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--ip))
- `producer_byte_rate` (Number) Maximum bytes per second the entity may publish, per broker. Must not be negative. Remove the attribute to remove the limit.
- `request_percentage` (Number) Maximum share of broker request handling time (network and I/O threads) the entity may use, as a percentage. Must not be negative. Remove the attribute to remove the limit.
- `user` (Attributes) The user (principal) the quota applies to. Can be combined with `client_id`, not with `ip`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--user))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Quota id, for example `user=alice,client-id=billing`, `ip=10.0.0.1` or `user=<default>`. Entity names are URL-escaped.

<a id="nestedatt--client_id"></a>
### Nested Schema for `client_id`

Optional:

- `default` (Boolean) Set to `true` to apply the quota to the default entity, which covers every entity of this type without a more specific quota. Set either `name` or `default`.
- `name` (String) Name of the entity. Set either `name` or `default`.


<a id="nestedatt--ip"></a>
### Nested Schema for `ip`

Optional:

- `default` (Boolean) Set to `true` to apply the quota to the default entity, which covers every entity of this type without a more specific quota. Set either `name` or `default`.
- `name` (String) Name of the entity. Set either `name` or `default`.


<a id="nestedatt--user"></a>
### Nested Schema for `user`

Optional:

- `default` (Boolean) Set to `true` to apply the quota to the default entity, which covers every entity of this type without a more specific quota. Set either `name` or `default`.
- `name` (String) Name of the entity. Set either `name` or `default`.
